items.stem: Explain the term “tetravalence of carbon”.
items.answer: The ability of carbon to form four covalent bonds.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the ability of carbon to form four covalent bonds.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about classification of organic compounds is correct?
items.answer: Members of a homologous series show a gradation in physical properties.
items.markingKey: (d) Members of a homologous series show a gradation in physical properties. The other statements are false. Members of a homologous series have the same functional group. Cyclohexane is an alicyclic (non-aromatic) compound. Hybridisation of carbon decides the shape (sp³ tetrahedral, sp² planar, sp linear).
options: Members of a homologous series have different functional groups.
In carbon compounds the shape of a molecule does not depend on hybridisation.
Members of a homologous series show a gradation in physical properties.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT an aldehyde?
items.answer: CH₃CH₂OH
items.markingKey: (a) CH₃CH₂OH is an alcohol, not an aldehyde.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Cyclohexane is an aromatic compound.”
items.answer: Cyclohexane is an alicyclic (non-aromatic) compound.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Cyclohexane is an alicyclic (non-aromatic) compound.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Carbon forms a very large number of compounds.
Reason (R): Carbon shows catenation and forms strong C–C bonds as well as multiple bonds.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Catenation and multiple bonding allow countless chains and rings.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Why is the molecular mass difference between successive members of a homologous series always 14 u?
items.answer: Successive members differ by one –CH₂– unit, whose mass is 12 + 2 × 1 = 14 u.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: CH₂; 1 mark: 14 u.

items.stem: Which term describes a series of organic compounds with the same functional group in which successive members differ by a –CH₂– unit?
items.answer: a homologous series
items.markingKey: (c) A homologous series: a series of organic compounds with the same functional group in which successive members differ by a –CH₂– unit.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about classification of organic compounds is incorrect?
items.answer: Cyclohexane is an aromatic compound.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “Cyclohexane is an aromatic compound.” Correct form: Cyclohexane is an alicyclic (non-aromatic) compound.
options: In the bond-line formula of propane only two lines are drawn.
Carbon forms four covalent bonds because it has four valence electrons.
Pyridine is a heterocyclic aromatic compound.

items.stem: Ethanol and dimethyl ether have the same molecular formula C₂H₆O. To which classes do they belong and how do their structures differ?
items.answer: Ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH) is an alcohol with an –OH group; dimethyl ether (CH₃OCH₃) is an ether with C–O–C. They are functional isomers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: classes; 1 mark: structural difference / functional isomerism.

items.stem: Which of the following is an aldehyde?
items.answer: CH₃CHO
items.markingKey: (d) CH₃CHO is an aldehyde; the others are not.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT an acyclic (open-chain) compound?
items.answer: tetrahydrofuran (as a cyclic ether)
items.markingKey: (d) Tetrahydrofuran (as a cyclic ether) is an alicyclic compound, not an acyclic (open-chain) compound.

items.stem: What is meant by “structural isomers”?
items.answer: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about IUPAC nomenclature and isomerism is correct?
items.answer: The suffix for a ketone is “-one”.
items.markingKey: (a) The suffix for a ketone is “-one”. The other statements are false. It is 2-methylbutane; the chain is numbered to give the lowest locant. The suffix for aldehydes is “-al”; “-ol” is for alcohols. They are chain isomers.
options: The suffix for a ketone is “-one”.
The IUPAC name of CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃ is 3-methylbutane.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The suffix for a ketone is “-one”.
Reason (R): The IUPAC name of CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃ is 3-methylbutane.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: It is 2-methylbutane; the chain is numbered to give the lowest locant.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Butane and 2-methylpropane are position isomers.”
items.answer: They are chain isomers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: They are chain isomers.

items.stem: What type of isomerism is shown by pentane and 2-methylbutane?
items.answer: chain isomerism
items.markingKey: (a) Pentane and 2-methylbutane: chain isomerism.

items.stem: How many structural isomers are possible for the molecular formula C₃H₈O? Name them.
items.answer: 3: propan-1-ol, propan-2-ol, methoxyethane
items.markingKey: 3 isomers (1 mark); naming them: propan-1-ol, propan-2-ol, methoxyethane (1 mark).

items.stem: A student named CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂CH₃ as 4-methylhexane. Identify the error and give the correct name.
items.answer: The chain was numbered from the wrong end; numbering must give the substituent the lowest locant: 3-methylhexane.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: lowest-locant rule; 1 mark: 3-methylhexane.

items.stem: For the molecular formula C₄H₈O: (a) draw (write) an aldehyde and a ketone and name them; (b) name the type of isomerism between them; (c) write one more aldehyde isomer and state its relation to the first; (d) give one chemical test to distinguish the aldehyde from the ketone.
items.answer: (a) Butanal CH₃CH₂CH₂CHO; butan-2-one CH₃COCH₂CH₃. (b) Functional group isomerism. (c) 2-methylpropanal (CH₃)₂CHCHO – chain isomer of butanal. (d) Tollens' reagent gives a silver mirror with the aldehyde, not the ketone.
items.markingKey: (a) 2 marks (b) 1 mark (c) 1 mark (d) 1 mark.

items.stem: Which term describes the functional group chosen as the suffix when a compound has more than one functional group?
items.answer: the principal functional group
items.markingKey: (b) The principal functional group: the functional group chosen as the suffix when a compound has more than one functional group.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about IUPAC nomenclature and isomerism is incorrect?
items.answer: Propanal and propanone are position isomers.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “Propanal and propanone are position isomers.” Correct form: They are functional group isomers.
options: Propanal and propanone are position isomers.
Ethanol and dimethyl ether are functional isomers.
Pentane has three chain isomers including itself.
–COOH has higher priority than –OH in choosing the suffix.

items.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₂=CHCN?
items.answer: prop-2-enenitrile
items.markingKey: (d) Select the longest chain containing the functional group/multiple bond, number to give lowest locants: prop-2-enenitrile.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol are position isomers.
Reason (R): They differ only in the position of the –OH group on the same carbon chain.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Same chain and group, different position.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Define the term “the principal functional group”.
items.answer: The functional group chosen as the suffix when a compound has more than one functional group.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the functional group chosen as the suffix when a compound has more than one functional group.

items.stem: What is meant by “the electromeric effect”?
items.answer: A temporary, complete transfer of a shared pair of π-electrons to one atom in the presence of an attacking reagent.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a temporary, complete transfer of a shared pair of π-electrons to one atom in the presence of an attacking reagent.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as electrophile or nucleophile: RO⁻, NO₂⁺, NH₃, AlCl₃.
items.answer: RO⁻ – nucleophile; NO₂⁺ – electrophile; NH₃ – nucleophile; AlCl₃ – electrophile.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: RO⁻ – nucleophile; NO₂⁺ – electrophile; NH₃ – nucleophile; AlCl₃ – electrophile.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Primary carbocations are more stable than tertiary ones.
Reason (R): Hyperconjugation is also called no-bond resonance.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Tertiary carbocations are most stable due to +I and hyperconjugation. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Carbanions are electron-deficient species.”
items.answer: Carbanions carry an extra lone pair; carbocations are electron deficient.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Carbanions carry an extra lone pair; carbocations are electron deficient.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about electronic displacements in covalent bonds is incorrect?
items.answer: The inductive effect increases with distance from the substituent.
items.markingKey: (d) The incorrect statement is “The inductive effect increases with distance from the substituent.” Correct form: It decreases rapidly with distance and is negligible beyond three bonds.
options: Tertiary carbocations are more stable than primary ones.
In a carbocation the positive carbon is sp² hybridised.
Hyperconjugation is also called no-bond resonance.
The inductive effect increases with distance from the substituent.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): (CH₃)₃C⁺ is more stable than CH₃CH₂⁺.
Reason (R): The tert-butyl cation has nine α-hydrogens for hyperconjugation.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) More hyperconjugation spreads the positive charge.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Explain why the electron-withdrawing –NO₂ group makes p-nitrophenol a stronger acid than phenol.
items.answer: –NO₂ withdraws electrons by −I and −R effects, delocalising the negative charge of the phenoxide ion onto the nitro group and stabilising it; a more stable conjugate base means a stronger acid.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: −R/−I effect; 1 mark: stabilisation of phenoxide ion.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct increasing order of acid strength: CH₃COOH, ClCH₂COOH, Cl₃CCOOH, Cl₂CHCOOH. Give a reason.
items.answer: CH₃COOH < ClCH₂COOH < Cl₂CHCOOH < Cl₃CCOOH
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order CH₃COOH < ClCH₂COOH < Cl₂CHCOOH < Cl₃CCOOH; 1 mark for the reason: Each Cl adds −I effect, stabilising the carboxylate ion.

items.stem: How many α-hydrogen atoms (hyperconjugable C–H bonds) are present in CH₃⁺ (methyl carbocation)?
items.markingKey: Count C–H bonds on carbon atoms directly attached to the positive carbon / sp² carbon: 0. More α-H means more hyperconjugative stabilisation.

items.stem: Which of the following is an electrophile?
items.answer: CH₃CO⁺
items.markingKey: (d) CH₃CO⁺ is an electrophile; the others are not.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as group showing +R (electron-releasing resonance) effect or group showing −R (electron-withdrawing resonance) effect: –CHO, –CN, –NH₂, –OH.
items.answer: –CHO – group showing −R (electron-withdrawing resonance) effect; –CN – group showing −R (electron-withdrawing resonance) effect; –NH₂ – group showing +R (electron-releasing resonance) effect; –OH – group showing +R (electron-releasing resonance) effect.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: –CHO – group showing −R (electron-withdrawing resonance) effect; –CN – group showing −R (electron-withdrawing resonance) effect; –NH₂ – group showing +R (electron-releasing resonance) effect; –OH – group showing +R (electron-releasing resonance) effect.

items.stem: What is meant by “hyperconjugation”?
items.answer: The delocalisation of σ-electrons of a C–H bond of an alkyl group attached to an unsaturated atom or a carbocation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the delocalisation of σ-electrons of a C–H bond of an alkyl group attached to an unsaturated atom or a carbocation.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a group showing +R (electron-releasing resonance) effect?
items.answer: –CN
items.markingKey: (b) –CN is a group showing −R (electron-withdrawing resonance) effect, not a group showing +R (electron-releasing resonance) effect.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct increasing order of acid strength?
items.answer: ClCH₂COOH < Cl₂CHCOOH < Cl₃CCOOH
items.markingKey: (d) ClCH₂COOH < Cl₂CHCOOH < Cl₃CCOOH. Each Cl adds −I effect, stabilising the carboxylate ion.

items.stem: Define the term “a rearrangement reaction”.
items.answer: A reaction in which atoms or groups of a molecule are rearranged to give a new structure.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a reaction in which atoms or groups of a molecule are rearranged to give a new structure.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about types of organic reactions is correct?
items.answer: Homolytic fission produces free radicals.
items.markingKey: (c) Homolytic fission produces free radicals. The other statements are false. It is an elimination reaction. Free radicals are neutral species with an unpaired electron. Alkanes undergo substitution; addition is typical of unsaturated compounds.
options: Dehydration of ethanol to ethene is a substitution reaction.
Free radicals carry a positive charge.
Addition reactions are typical of alkanes.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT an addition reaction?
items.answer: CH₂BrCH₂Br + Zn → CH₂=CH₂ + ZnBr₂
items.markingKey: (d) CH₂BrCH₂Br + Zn → CH₂=CH₂ + ZnBr₂ is an elimination reaction, not an addition reaction.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Heterolytic fission produces free radicals.”
items.answer: Heterolytic fission produces ions; homolytic fission produces radicals.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Heterolytic fission produces ions; homolytic fission produces radicals.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Chlorination of methane requires sunlight or heat.
Reason (R): Energy is needed for homolytic fission of the Cl–Cl bond into chlorine free radicals.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Light provides energy to start the free radical chain.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Why are carbocations formed more easily in polar solvents?
items.answer: Heterolytic fission produces ions; polar solvents stabilise the ions by solvation, lowering the energy needed for the fission.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: heterolysis gives ions; 1 mark: solvation stabilises them.

items.stem: Which of the following is a rearrangement reaction?
items.answer: NH₄CNO → NH₂CONH₂ (on heating)
items.markingKey: (c) NH₄CNO → NH₂CONH₂ (on heating) is a rearrangement reaction; the others are not.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between heterolytic fission and homolytic fission on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A bond in a reaction breaks in this way: shown with half-headed (fish-hook) arrows. Identify the type of bond fission – heterolytic fission or homolytic fission? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Heterolytic fission: one atom keeps both electrons of the bonding pair; a carbocation and an anion (or carbanion and cation) are formed; favoured by polar solvents. Homolytic fission: each atom keeps one electron of the bonding pair; free radicals are formed; favoured by heat, light or peroxides and non-polar solvents. (b) Homolytic fission.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: homolytic fission; 1 mark: “shown with half-headed (fish-hook) arrows” is a feature of homolytic fission.

items.stem: A bond in a reaction breaks in this way: shown with full-headed curved arrows; one atom keeps both electrons of the bonding pair; favoured by polar solvents. Identify the type of bond fission. Give a reason.
items.answer: Heterolytic fission
items.markingKey: 1 mark: heterolytic fission; 1 mark: the features shown with full-headed curved arrows; one atom keeps both electrons of the bonding pair; favoured by polar solvents are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
A bond in a reaction breaks in this way: favoured by polar solvents; one atom keeps both electrons of the bonding pair; a carbocation and an anion (or carbanion and cation) are formed.
(i) Identify the type of bond fission. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were homolytic fission? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Heterolytic fission (ii) shown with full-headed curved arrows (iii) each atom keeps one electron of the bonding pair; free radicals are formed
items.markingKey: (i) heterolytic fission – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: shown with full-headed curved arrows – 1 mark. (iii) for homolytic fission: each atom keeps one electron of the bonding pair; free radicals are formed; favoured by heat, light or peroxides and non-polar solvents – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Classify CH₃CH₂Br + KOH(aq) → CH₃CH₂OH + KBr and CH₃CH₂Br + KOH(alc) → CH₂=CH₂ + KBr + H₂O, and explain why the same reagents give different reactions.
items.answer: The first is substitution (OH⁻ acts as nucleophile in aqueous medium); the second is elimination (alcoholic KOH gives the stronger base alkoxide/OH⁻ that removes β-H).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: classification; 1 mark: role of solvent/reagent behaviour.

items.stem: Explain the term “Lassaigne's test”.
items.answer: Detection of N, S, P and halogens by converting them into ionic sodium compounds by fusing the organic compound with sodium.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: detection of N, S, P and halogens by converting them into ionic sodium compounds by fusing the organic compound with sodium.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about purification and analysis of organic compounds is correct?
items.answer: In the Kjeldahl method nitrogen is converted into ammonium sulphate.
items.markingKey: (b) In the Kjeldahl method nitrogen is converted into ammonium sulphate. The other statements are false. It does not work for nitro, azo compounds and nitrogen in a ring (pyridine). Glycerol decomposes at its boiling point; it is distilled under reduced pressure. CO₂ is absorbed in KOH; water is absorbed in anhydrous CaCl₂.
options: In Liebig's method CO₂ is absorbed in anhydrous CaCl₂.
In the Kjeldahl method nitrogen is converted into ammonium sulphate.
Glycerol is purified by simple distillation.
Kjeldahl's method works for all organic nitrogen compounds.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Glycerol is purified by simple distillation.
Reason (R): Kjeldahl's method is not applicable to nitro compounds, azo compounds and pyridine.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Glycerol decomposes at its boiling point; it is distilled under reduced pressure. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Kjeldahl's method works for all organic nitrogen compounds.”
items.answer: It does not work for nitro, azo compounds and nitrogen in a ring (pyridine).
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: It does not work for nitro, azo compounds and nitrogen in a ring (pyridine).

items.stem: In Lassaigne's test the sodium fusion extract shows: a violet colour with sodium nitroprusside; formation of Na₂S during fusion. Which element is present?
items.answer: sulphur
items.markingKey: (c) Sulphur: a violet colour with sodium nitroprusside; formation of Na₂S during fusion.

items.stem:
A mixture or compound has these properties: used to separate aniline from an aniline–water mixture; the mixture boils below 373 K because the vapour pressures add.
(i) Which method of purification is most suitable? (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were simple distillation? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Steam distillation (ii) the compound is steam volatile and immiscible with water (iii) two liquids differ widely in boiling points (e.g. chloroform 334 K and aniline 457 K); the liquids do not decompose at their boiling points
items.markingKey: (i) steam distillation – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: the compound is steam volatile and immiscible with water – 1 mark. (iii) for simple distillation: two liquids differ widely in boiling points (e.g. chloroform 334 K and aniline 457 K); the liquids do not decompose at their boiling points; the vapour of the lower-boiling liquid is condensed first – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: In Sahil's paper chromatography experiment the solvent front moved 7.4 cm and a coloured spot moved 4.1 cm from the base line. Calculate the Rf value of the component.
items.markingKey: Rf = distance moved by substance / distance moved by solvent front = 4.1/7.4 = 0.55.

items.stem: A mixture or compound has these properties: the compound is steam volatile and immiscible with water; used to separate aniline from an aniline–water mixture. Which method of purification is most suitable? Give a reason.
items.answer: Steam distillation
items.markingKey: 1 mark: steam distillation; 1 mark: the features the compound is steam volatile and immiscible with water; used to separate aniline from an aniline–water mixture are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
In Lassaigne's test the sodium fusion extract shows: formation of sodium thiocyanate (NaSCN); a blood-red colour with FeCl₃.
(i) Which element is present? (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were nitrogen? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Nitrogen and sulphur together (ii) no Prussian blue because the cyanide is used up as thiocyanate (iii) a Prussian blue colour with FeSO₄ and then FeCl₃ in acid; formation of sodium cyanide during fusion
items.markingKey: (i) nitrogen and sulphur together – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: no Prussian blue because the cyanide is used up as thiocyanate – 1 mark. (iii) for nitrogen: a Prussian blue colour with FeSO₄ and then FeCl₃ in acid; formation of sodium cyanide during fusion; Fe₄[Fe(CN)₆]₃ formed – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: In Lassaigne's test the sodium fusion extract shows: a precipitate with AgNO₃ after boiling with HNO₃; yellowish precipitate sparingly soluble in NH₄OH for bromine. Which element is present? Give a reason.
items.answer: A halogen
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a halogen; 1 mark: the features a precipitate with AgNO₃ after boiling with HNO₃; yellowish precipitate sparingly soluble in NH₄OH for bromine are characteristic of it.

items.stem: In the Carius method, 0.20 g of an organic compound gave 0.429 g of AgCl. Calculate the percentage of chlorine in the compound.
On complete combustion, 0.30 g of an organic compound gave 0.440 g of CO₂ and 0.180 g of H₂O. Calculate the percentage of carbon and hydrogen in it.
Which of the following statements about electronic displacements in covalent bonds is correct?
items.answer: The electromeric effect is temporary and operates only in the presence of a reagent.
items.markingKey: (d) The electromeric effect is temporary and operates only in the presence of a reagent. The other statements are false. Tertiary carbocations are most stable due to +I and hyperconjugation. Carbanions carry an extra lone pair; carbocations are electron deficient. It decreases rapidly with distance and is negligible beyond three bonds.
options: The inductive effect increases with distance from the substituent.
Primary carbocations are more stable than tertiary ones.
The electromeric effect is temporary and operates only in the presence of a reagent.

items.stem: Which term describes a reaction in which two atoms or groups are removed from a molecule, usually forming a multiple bond?
items.answer: an elimination reaction
items.markingKey: (a) An elimination reaction: a reaction in which two atoms or groups are removed from a molecule, usually forming a multiple bond.

items.stem:
A mixture or compound has these properties: two liquids have boiling points close to each other; used to separate crude oil fractions.
(i) Which method of purification is most suitable? (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were steam distillation? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Fractional distillation (ii) a fractionating column is used (iii) used to separate aniline from an aniline–water mixture; the mixture boils below 373 K because the vapour pressures add
items.markingKey: (i) fractional distillation – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: a fractionating column is used – 1 mark. (iii) for steam distillation: the compound is steam volatile and immiscible with water; used to separate aniline from an aniline–water mixture; the mixture boils below 373 K because the vapour pressures add – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The suffix for aldehydes is “-ol”.”
items.answer: The suffix for aldehydes is “-al”; “-ol” is for alcohols.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The suffix for aldehydes is “-al”; “-ol” is for alcohols.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as elimination reaction or addition reaction: CH₃CH₂Br + KOH(alc) → CH₂=CH₂ + KBr + H₂O, CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ → CH₃CH₃ (Ni), CH₂BrCH₂Br + Zn → CH₂=CH₂ + ZnBr₂, CH₃CHO + HCN → CH₃CH(OH)CN.
items.answer: CH₃CH₂Br + KOH(alc) → CH₂=CH₂ + KBr + H₂O – elimination reaction; CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ → CH₃CH₃ (Ni) – addition reaction; CH₂BrCH₂Br + Zn → CH₂=CH₂ + ZnBr₂ – elimination reaction; CH₃CHO + HCN → CH₃CH(OH)CN – addition reaction.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: CH₃CH₂Br + KOH(alc) → CH₂=CH₂ + KBr + H₂O – elimination reaction; CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ → CH₃CH₃ (Ni) – addition reaction; CH₂BrCH₂Br + Zn → CH₂=CH₂ + ZnBr₂ – elimination reaction; CH₃CHO + HCN → CH₃CH(OH)CN – addition reaction.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about purification and analysis of organic compounds is incorrect?
items.answer: In Liebig's method CO₂ is absorbed in anhydrous CaCl₂.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “In Liebig's method CO₂ is absorbed in anhydrous CaCl₂.” Correct form: CO₂ is absorbed in KOH; water is absorbed in anhydrous CaCl₂.
options: In Liebig's method CO₂ is absorbed in anhydrous CaCl₂.
Copper(II) oxide is used to oxidise carbon and hydrogen in Liebig's method.
In the Kjeldahl method nitrogen is converted into ammonium sulphate.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about classification of organic compounds is correct?
